title: Corrupting Ties: Investigating Robustness to Bias Injection Across Multi-Agent Network Topologies
abstract: arXiv:2611.21804v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness. We introduce a controlled bias injection framework that replaces selected agent responses with predefined biased ones, enabling an intervention-based analysis of how network topology and injection configurations shape system behavior. We propose decision divergence metrics that quantify the effects of these interventions at the agent, network, and system levels, and evaluate five topologies on three binary classification tasks using LLMs from the Qwen and Gemma families. translated_title: 腐蚀纽带：探究多智能体网络拓扑对偏见注入的鲁棒性
translated_abstract: AI系统正日益被部署于高风险决策场景中，其中组件间的交互可能引入公平性风险，而这种风险在单独审计组件或集体结果时往往无法被发现。随着基于LLM的多智能体系统日益普及，理解偏见信息如何在智能体交互中传播对于评估其公平性至关重要。我们提出了一种受控偏见注入框架，将选定的智能体响应替换为预定义的偏见响应，从而能够通过干预分析来考察网络拓扑和注入配置如何塑造系统行为。我们提出了决策分歧度量指标，在智能体、网络和系统层面量化这些干预的影响，并使用来自Qwen和Gemma系列的LLM在三个二分类任务上评估了五种拓扑结构。序列网络显示出最大的分歧，而全连接……
tldr: 该论文提出受控偏见注入框架与决策分歧度量指标，系统研究了多智能体网络拓扑对偏见传播的鲁棒性，发现序列网络受偏见注入影响产生的决策分歧最大。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a controlled bias injection framework and decision divergence metrics to systematically investigate the robustness of multi-agent network topologies to bias propagation, finding that sequential networks exhibit the greatest divergence.
